cm_single_fault.description: One CM / one RF station fault that produces a clean single-cavity collapse. Use these instead of quench propagation events for teaching the CM-to-beam-dump chain.

examples.why_clean: CM3 ARC interlock. ARC_CM3 is the first digital, only CM3 collapses, and CM1/CM2 only dip/oscillate.
examples.caution: The MCP measurement class is single_cavity_quench, but QUEN_CM3 did not assert; the actual fault is ARC.

examples.why_clean: KSU3 HVPS water flow low. RDY_KSU3 is the only interlock, CM3 collapses, and the remaining stations stay up.
examples.caution: This is a KSU/HPRF station fault, not a cavity quench.

ksu_single_station.description: KSU/HPRF internal fault on one station. The faulted station loses RF first; other stations compensate within the over-input limit.

examples.why_clean: KSU3 HVPS water flow low; clean single-station RF loss.
examples.caution: Do not call this a Kicker event; KSU is Klystron Supply Unit.

quench_propagation.description: Quench events are valid events but are poor canonical examples for 'one CM fault' because the waveform class can be rf_trip/mixed and multiple cavities may move.

examples.why_clean: Operator note says CM1 quench and QUEN_CM1 is the first digital.
examples.caution: Class=rf_trip, all 3 cavities eventually collapse, tau_reliable=false, and the CM2/CM3 10% times are +37 ms. Do not quote tau=17 ms, do not call the collapses simultaneous, and do not call this a clean single-CM example.
